To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
- First, migrants’ cultural integration is not a one-way street.

(i) migrants from the same origin group do not follow the same cultural integration trajectory, (ii) economic discrimination and cultural barriers to the economic integration of migrants reinforce each other, (iii) the more conservative political preferences of the German-speaking part of Switzerland do not affect the economic integration of migrant workers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the economic and cultural dimension of the integration process of migrants and their descendants in Switzerland.
the economic and cultural outcomes of migrant integration, with how they are related, and how host society culture influences these outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
migrant economic integration is hindered by discrimination and cultural barriers to the extent that they reinforce each other.
migrants’ integration is a complex and multi-faceted phenomenon that is not easily reducible to a simple causal relationship.
migrants are integrating into Swiss society, but not as fast as they could.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
migrants are not a homogeneous group, and that their integration paths differ according to their country of origin and their socio-demographic characteristics.
cultural differences do not prevent migrants from successfully integrating in Swiss society.
the integration of migrants into the host society is a long-term process that is influenced by a multitude of economic and cultural factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cultural dimension of integration is a key determinant of the economic dimension.
the economic and cultural aspects of migrant integration should not be studied separately.
the economic and cultural aspects of the integration process are interdependent.
